summary: Join our Training of Trainers (TOT) on Women in Leadership Course. Equip yourself to mentor and uplift women leaders in your organization and beyond.
lede: Women’s leadership trainer training helps professionals who train or support women leaders design and deliver sustained programmes. It develops skills in analyzing gender and power dynamics, structuring learning journeys, and facilitating inclusive discussions about bias and resistance. The syllabus also covers coaching and mentoring, plus ways to track participation, learning, and behavior change.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who train, mentor, or support women in leadership, and those mandated to drive gender and leadership initiatives. This course is designed for: Learning and development (L&D) professionals responsible for leadership programmes. HR and talent managers building women in leadership pipelines. Gender focal persons and gender equality officers. NGO and development practitioners running women's leadership or empowerment projects. Internal trainers and facilitators tasked with designing and delivering leadership sessions. Senior and mid-level women leaders who mentor other women and want stronger facilitation skills. Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) champions implementing gender initiatives. Consultants who design women in leadership academies or coaching programmes. Team leaders and supervisors who regularly run internal learning or coaching sessions. Anyone responsible for teaching, mentoring, or facilitating leadership growth for women.
modules: The Case for Women in Leadership
Foundations of Adult Learning for TOT
Understanding Gender, Power, and Leadership Dynamics
Facilitation Skills for Inclusive Learning Spaces
Coaching, Mentoring, and Sponsorship for Women Leaders
Content Topics for Women in Leadership Journeys
Handling Bias, Resistance, and Difficult Conversations
Measuring Impact of Women in Leadership Programmes
Action Planning and Trainer Development Pathways
prerequisites: Participants should have experience in training, facilitation, or leadership development roles. Familiarity with gender and leadership concepts is beneficial but not mandatory.
